changelog.change: Initial entry — interactive all-must-be-true checklist for the AAP 2016 lower-risk BRUE definition; complements the brue-pathway reference (which carries the full lower- and higher-risk management detail). Follow-on named in the brue-pathway build note.
Reformatted for reading on a phone: long paragraphs broken into short paragraphs and lists. Wording and clinical content unchanged.

purpose: Applies the AAP 2016 definition of a LOWER-RISK Brief Resolved Unexplained Event. A BRUE is a sudden, brief, now-resolved episode in an infant < 1 year of a color change, absent/decreased/irregular breathing, marked tone change, or altered responsiveness, with no explanation after a full history and exam. Every criterion below must be met to call it lower-risk; if any is not met, use the higher-risk framework.
ageRange: Infants < 1 year (BRUE is not defined outside this age)

embeddedCalculator.title: BRUE — Lower-Risk Criteria
embeddedCalculator.purpose: All seven criteria must be met for a lower-risk BRUE.

items.label: Born ≥ 32 weeks gestation AND postconceptional age ≥ 45 weeks
First BRUE (no prior BRUE, not occurring in clusters)
No CPR by a trained medical provider
No concerning physical examination findings (see notes)

interpretation.label: LOWER-RISK BRUE — all seven criteria met
interpretation.risk: In this group the risk of a serious underlying diagnosis or a recurrent event is low.
interpretation.disposition:
MAY:
- brief ED/observation monitoring with continuous pulse oximetry and serial exams
- 12-lead ECG
- test for pertussis

SHOULD NOT ROUTINELY:
- admit solely for monitoring
- send WBC/blood culture/CSF/chemistries/blood gas/ammonia/lactate/urine organic acids
- obtain CXR, echo, neuroimaging, EEG, or a skeletal survey
- start acid suppression or anti-epileptics
- discharge a home cardiorespiratory monitor

Shared decision-making with caregivers, offer CPR training resources, arrange follow-up within 24 h.

interpretation.label: NOT lower-risk — at least one criterion is not met
interpretation.risk: The event does not meet the AAP lower-risk definition; it does not by itself quantify how high the risk is.
interpretation.disposition: Use the higher-risk framework (Merritt 2019) in the brue-pathway module: targeted, feature-driven evaluation and a period of monitored observation rather than the broad ALTE work-up. Escalate for any explanation found on history/exam (that makes it an explained event, not a BRUE), prematurity, recurrent or clustered events, a family history of sudden unexplained death, social concern, or an abnormal exam.

embeddedCalculator.notes:
Concerning HISTORY (any present → not a simple lower-risk BRUE, and may point to a specific cause):
- recurrent events or events in clusters
- event during sleep vs feeding vs waking
- duration > 1 min
- required stimulation or resuscitation
- prior similar events
- possible non-accidental trauma, suffocation, or medication/toxin exposure
- family history of sudden unexplained death, cardiac disease, or metabolic/genetic disease
- social or environmental risk

Concerning EXAM (any present → evaluate further):
- abnormal vital signs or growth
- respiratory distress
- abnormal tone or neurologic exam
- murmur or abnormal cardiac exam
- organomegaly
- dysmorphology
- bruising/oral or ocular injury or other signs of abuse
- fever

body.text: A BRUE requires that the clinician finds NO explanation after a full history and exam. If a cause is identified (GERD with choking, a viral URI, a witnessed seizure, a toxic exposure, etc.) it is an explained event and is managed on its own merits — the BRUE pathway does not apply.

items: The evidence does not support hospitalization solely for cardiorespiratory monitoring, or a broad laboratory/imaging work-up.
Reasonable options: a short period of monitored observation with continuous pulse oximetry and serial exams; a 12-lead ECG; pertussis testing when exposure or cough is plausible.
Educate caregivers about BRUEs, offer CPR training resources, use shared decision-making, and ensure follow-up within 24 hours.
Do not routinely start acid suppression, prescribe anti-epileptic drugs, obtain neuroimaging or an EEG, or send home a cardiorespiratory monitor.

body.text: Move to the higher-risk framework in brue-pathway: it is expert consensus (not a validated rule) and pairs each risk-elevating feature with a targeted test rather than a reflex panel, plus a period of monitored observation and clear return precautions.

buildNote: peds-tool with an embedded additive calculator — 7 criteria, all-must-be-true (score 7/7 = lower-risk). The concerning-history and concerning-exam feature lists live in the calculator notes and the body. Defers to brue-pathway for the full lower- and higher-risk management detail. Follow-on named in the brue-pathway build note.
